notes: Actual results reported to the State Comptroller for the fiscal year ending 2026-05-31, not an adopted budget.
Covers the village government only. Village residents also pay the town that surrounds Turin, which is listed separately, plus county and school taxes.
Employee benefits ($4,570) are spread across departments in proportion to their size.

Political money counts PAC, business and union contributions to candidates for Village of Turin offices reported to the State Board of Elections since 2022-10-01. Individual donors ($0 in the same period), candidates' own committees and party committees are not counted. Campaigns that raise little may not itemize, so some contributions may not appear.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-01. Data center deals and corporate lobbying come from a hand-checked list of news reports and public records. A town with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
